notes.title: Bruni Multimedia is now Dodonovels
notes.content:
Greetings fellow players and doctors!

Recently, I was presented with an engaging opportunity that necessitated a shift in my current life. As such, I had to part ways with Bruni Multimedia and pass on the rights of ownership for all games and their licenses to another entity. Although this decision wasn't easy for me to make, it has opened up many doors of potential success moving forward.

Dodonovels is the new entity which will own all of my games in the future.With the idea of rebranding in mind, I believe now is an ideal moment to create a new name and logo for my games.

Updates and patches for all the games have been delayed a lot for this reason, and I apologize for that. With confidence, I will now take the lead again and you can anticipate more releases and content to come shortly. This is even with a few collaborations from some of the people who responded positively to my request for help that I issued only weeks ago.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33586573/32df42671ea1537e9965d1f1001ce7853d3b758d.png[/img]

[b]What is going to change for the games?[/b]
Absolutely nothing, except that bug fixing and new content will be once more made available faster and sooner.

[b]Does this mean you're no longer involved in the projects?[/b]
No, I'm still very much involved. The same development and ideas are still at the wheel and will continue to provide support for each game as usual. Something will change especially in General Practitioner 2, and the game will receive more and more content.

[b]Do you still need our help?[/b]
Of course I do! Crowdfunding and early access is of fundamental importance for very small indie studios like Dodonovels, and the future success and release of the games depends on how well they're received and supported by the public. Without your help , it would be impossible to make all projects a reality.

Thank you for your trust and support during this transition period. It has been an amazing journey so far and I'm looking forward to what the future holds!

Sincerely,

Andrea

notes.title: Yomi Alliance will leave Early Access this month!
notes.content:
Greetings fellow space officers.

First and foremost, Yomi Alliance is set to exit Early Access this month with the final missions and the conclusion of the main characters' tales. 

This project has been particularly unlucky since it was scheduled for a full release in June 2021, including a comprehensive voice-over by many talented artists led by Star Trek veteran Manu Intiraymi who is still working with us on this project.

Despite this, Yomi emerged just as the Covid-19 pandemic was beginning, causing delays and a severe cash shortage that necessitated some cut features in order to bring the game out. I felt that the most essential aspect of a Visual Novel is the story, and I was behind schedule on that as well, owing to economic and financial challenges it had to overcome..

To make things worse, the disaster had a double edge: because of my previous work in other VNs and the general public following us, it was impossible to solely focus on Yomi release. The public following us appreciates General Practitioner and the other VNs as well, therefore I also had to develop something different at the same time.

However, I had to make tough calls regarding the game and it will not be in Early Access for a long time, so I was compelled to eliminate the voice-over program and only feature Manu Mkrell's portrait in select dialogues. This pains me far more than you can imagine, but after two years of severe financial strain, I had to choose between releasing the game or leaving it permanently in Alpha Early Access.

The in-game material will not be removed from the game's definitive version, except for voice overs: the tale will be concluded; numerous HD pictures and hours of gameplay will be included; bugs will be fixed, as well as new missions.

I would like to express my gratitude for your support, as it allowed me to pursue this project!

Thank you for continuing to support our games, I appreciate it very much. Thank you for keeping safe out there! Thank you for staying with us!

notes.title: Yomi Alliance 0.0.26: The Eye of God
notes.content:
Greetings, fellow space officers! 

It has been a long time coming, but I am finally ready to unveil the new content for Yomi Alliance. This update is packed with new features that will take the game to the next level. Players can look forward to an all-new sci-fi visual novel experience, complete with exciting quests and storylines! I cannot wait to see what you all think of it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/31352b19a170aa7fc3269f54df8adfe651e3a817.jpg[/img]

In this brand new mission, you have been ordered to Rilvupra IV, a colony that is revered by many different species. The planet is a destination of pilgrimage for people from many different civilizations, and the problem lies there. Because various religions consider the location holy, there are numerous conflicts due to the differences in their beliefs. 

Tensions have recently grown worse. A more militant group of pilgrims has taken to violence, reasserting a new "Prophet" to guide them to Heaven, instead of the "False God" that is worshipped on Rilvupra.

You'll see that the world is actually a highly telepathic self-aware entity that has come to the conclusion that it must be "the god" the people worship and that an holy apocalypse might help to resolve its crisis of faith, even by destroying the Kressari who claims to be the genuine "Prophet," and the Nixanti believing in their own God, Alarei.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/905b26c77af204fc1b401f8a9684eb243ca1a130.jpg[/img]

Can you persuade the entity that it isn't a god, even though it appears to match the description of one? 

Can you prevent the galaxy from descending into all-out war? This is only the beginning of your journey. 

With new areas to discover and tales to hear, Yomi Alliance 0.0.26 is getting closer and closer to its Beta. Get onboard and assist the team!

"The Eye of God" will be available in a few weeks! Keep following us!

notes.title: Yomi Alliance will receive a MAJOR update in a few days!
notes.content:
Greetings fellow space officers.

It has been a while since the last update for Yomi Alliance, and that's because of previously stated personal and family issues which I still have to sort out completely. Still, I have released two different games in the meantime and also an episode for The Coroner Saga (Episode 5 is on its way too and I have a huge, nice surprise for Episode 6 which will close the season).

But we're here to talk about Yomi Alliance, today, and it's going to receive a HUGE update.

I started to look at the game's data a few months ago and noticed that most of the players were not choosing many careers as I thought. Most of you stick with the most "famous" ones, and this led to many, many hours of scripting and gameplay that was not ultimately enjoyed unless you replayed the game again and again, which is very unlikely according to the stats.

So I decided to remove sub-careers and make only primary ones available, such as:
[list]
[*] Command
[*] Science
[*] Security
[*] Operations
[*] Counseling
[*] Medical
[*] Engineering
[/list]

This won't mean you will lose different sub-missions or anything, just that you will access more content, special abilities and missions right from your first playthrough, with a lot of such content releasing over the next update.

[b]In the next update you can expect to find a lot of sub-stories, different missions and interactions with your crewmates.[/b]

Unfortunately, this will also mean that[b] you wlil have to start a new game[/b] once updated, because of these changes affecting the way the game works. Loading a previous game might result in bugs, unexpected behavior and crashes, so you are warned.

I always try to keep the need of restarting a new game as low as possible, but with the changes I made, this time, it will be impossible. The changes are also the reason because the update took so long, since I have to rethink about the whole game experience, but that's what alphas are for, after all.

Your feedback, your help and support are making this possible. And I plan to release a beta of the game in a few months, with the final release planned very soon while I finish writing the story, adding images, sexual content and voiceovers, which will cover the most important parts of the game.

I hope you'll enjoy the game as it releases and I hope to see you out there, in outer space!

Stay safe and healthy!

ANDREA

notes.title: Next update to feature the end of "Academy Days"
notes.content:
Greetings fellow officers!

Even though the situation is still very difficult, work on Yomi Alliance has only slowed down, but it never stopped. Today I'm proud to announce you that the next big update for the game, available in late May, will feature the end of "Academy Days", the first part of this adventure.

This will mean that every story arc will be available and concluded, every different mission objective for each career will be released and your characters will be introduced to "Graduation Day", which will be this summer's update!

[b]Wait, does it mean the game is completed?[/b]
Of course not! The first 24 weeks at the Academy will be only the beginning of the game. As I fix bugs, apply your suggestions and watch your feedback, the real story of Yomi Alliance will unfold update after update.

[b]The first part of the game is fun, but repetitive. If I want to try the second part of the game without having to play the first one again, will I be able to do so?[/b]

Of course! A new character creation will be made available for those who want to try the 2nd part of the game without having to go through the Academy. Of course, remember to choose different careers to unlock different scenarios.

[b]PART II – Officer Life[/b]
You graduated from the Academy and assigned to the [i]Y.S.S. Oraga[/i], a state-of-the-art recon vessel commanded by Vessel Captain Marston. All your fellow recruits have been promoted and assigned to the Oraga. Some of the instructors were also hand-picked by Captain Marston for the ship's roster.

Players will have different tasks depending on their career choice, so each story will play differently in content during the six missions of Part II. 

The following is the general plot of Part 2, without a detailed career path.
[b]Mission 1[/b]	
The Oraga responds to a distress call from a Nixanti freighter which is under attack by Kressari Forces inside Alliance Space. Upon interception the Kressari claim the freighter hosts dangerous Nixanti terrorists who fled from a high-security detention world. The Nixanti are freed after a confrontation (either by diplomacy or battle) and granted the request for protection. One of the rescued people is a young Kressari who recognizes the player as the Doombringer of her past visions. She also claims the planet Hurwada II is the staging ground for an Alliance invasion of Kressa.

[b]Mission 2[/b]	
Captain Marston orders to investigate the reports about Hurwada II. After arriving at the planet the Oraga is hailed by Fuminoid Administrator 9T37 who asks them to leave as the entire planet is under military secrecy. Captain Marston asks the player to investigate with an Away Team but is then forced to leave the sector when Fuminoid ships arrive in force.
 
[b]Mission 3[/b]	
Jerath Station, a Human scientific facility, is attacked by unknown assailants. The Oraga is dispatched to investigate. The attacking vessel is unknown but trace elements leave the crew to suspect Nixanti involvement. The vessel disappeared from sensors as it possessed something like a "cloaking device", but this technology is not known to exist in Alliance space, nor in the neighboring empires.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/2deb0c244e6358310406a1eb6a3b454c221a50f7.png[/img]

[b]Mission 4[/b]	
The Oraga investigates the disappearance of prominent human scientist Rachel Orlais, who was apparently kidnapped while on leave to Bujuri Prime with her husband, who has been killed in a brutal way. Investigations made by the player might lead to link Orlais' work to an ominous Fuminoid sect called "The Keepers of Time", whose agenda is unknown even by Fuminoid government.

[b]Mission 5[/b]	
Following the trail of the Keepers of Time the Oraga arrives to the planet Jubinai V, home to a remote colony of Nixanti and Fuminoids who established it way before the Yomi Treaty was signed. Completely unaware of the Alliance and their own species' recent history, the colonists referring themselves as "Fuminanti" have formed a cult around the figure of the "Doombringer". Upon investigating further, the Oraga crew discovers ancient texts referring to an "Artifact" in deep space who could empower its owner with god-like powers. The Artifact was built during the Nixanti-Fuminoid wars in 230 BY (Before Yomi) to force peace between the two warring factions, but it was never used as the two species met with Humans in a First Contact that ultimately led to the creation of Yomi Alliance. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/a10a6b80f09ee541082f0eb51e89ec69a26d8f48.jpg[/img]

I will not spoil the other 5 missions and the final one.
Each mission will be played differently as different career path are chosen. If you are a security guard expect some heavy fighting, while you can try (and save countless lives) by choosing to be a diplomat. As a Doctor, on the other hand, you might be called to save the life of Captain Marston, whose life could mean the difference between a full scale conflict between the Nixanti and the Fuminoid.

Expect some heavy story-driven concept in May's update, as we prepare to end Academy days. Your romantic interest will also play a role in determine the fate of the galaxy, but I cannot (and don't want) to spoil more.

Thanks for following this project! I hope you'll enjoy the new content!

notes.title: A statement regarding the current state of the game
notes.content:
Greetings guys!

First of all, thank you for your constant feedback about General Practioner and its issues. I am aware someone believes I abandoned the game, but that is NOT the case. However, I remind you that I'm working on this project on my own, and that there is no studio supporting my work as it relies on players only.

That said, I'm receiving reports I'm going to address, so you know what's going on right now.

[b]GAME NOT STARTING[/b]
Some of you complied about the game not starting overnight. I already tried to start the game from Steam myself, and it works fine. It looks like some configurations have had issues when starting the game, and I'm working on understanding what's going on. [b]You understand that with NO ERROR REPORTS nor every available computer, it is going to take some time for me to understand the issue[/b], which only affects a very rare minority of people, as right now some hundreds of you are playing it (if it was an issue with the game I would have 100% refunds AND 0 people playing, which is not happening).

[b]THE GAME ENGINE[/b]
As many Visual Novels, General Practitioner is written in Ren'Py, which has been recently updated to its latest patch. This might have caused some issues, which caused me to revert to the previous GP's patch. While I apologize for the issue this caused to some of you, I cannot speed up the process of releasing a patch for the engine, as I'm not its proprietor.
I am going to recompile it once more and release a small fix for both GP and Yomi Alliance, and I WILL NEED YOUR REPORTS to know if it's fixing the problem (with achievements as well). Steam also changed its integrated library recently.

As usual, you do understand this huge game has been made by myself only, so I rely on the documentation from both Steam and Ren'Py to make it work. It's entirely in my skills, but it will take some time.

[b]MISSING FILES[/b]
Every time you check for the file integrity you get 100+ files "missing" or needed to be redownloaded. [b][u]THIS IS WORKING AS INTENDED [/u][/b]because of the game's engine, as it writes temporary files every time the game is launched, which of course then differs from the ones in Steam's main repository. This doesn't cause ANY issue with the game, it's not a bug, nor it affects anything, and doesn't mean the game is broken in any way. When you leave a negative review about it, remind that you are basically telling people my game's bad because of some temporary files. You are free to check that the same happens with every ren'py-based Visual Novel out there.

[b]COVID IN ITALY[/b]
The current situation with COVID-19 restrictions in italy severely impacts on my family, thus making it harder to to everything in time. I had to reschedule my next game's launch, a couple patches with Yomi Alliance and voice actors, the creation of my Patreon page AND General Practitioner's next FREE update. I apologize for this, I truly do, but I don't know how to make it better, since it's not my choice to lock us away like they're doing.

[b]This also [u]hugely [/u]impacted my earnings[/b], as well as many people out there. My studio is VERY small (myself only) but I feed my family with it, and of course the budget for my next games (a new Unity-based engine, CGI, interactions) was impacted as well. I was going to launch a kickstarter for my newest projects, but that's out of the question now, since everyone is having a hard time because of the pandemic.

[b]DELAYS AND REFUNDS[/b]
I apologize for any delay in my projects. And I would understand if you like a refund for the game. You can always contact me in my email development[at]brunimultimedia.com, [b]if you disliked the game A LOT, leaving a negative review even after 100+ hours and Steam won't refund it, contact me and I'll send you money via Paypal.[/b]

[u][b]I started this job to entertain people and form a nice community around my games, not to fool them or take their money without giving anything in return. 
[/b][/u]
Even if you liked my game but still want a refund, be my guest. Really.

notes.title: Combat System overhaul
notes.content:
Greetings fellow space officers.

One of biggest prides is to always listen to players' feedback, and whenever it's possible to try and add to the game what they suggest and ask. 

That's why I started working on a [b]Combat System overhaul[/b] for the game.

Let's say it: the combat system used right now it's not fun, and sucks more than a little. Of course, [b]being the game in Alpha stage[/b] allows me to completely redo it from scratch, and with some new nice features.

First of all, [b]you will have full control on the action[/b], by choosing which kind of attack to perform, which weapon to use and also if and how to use special powers and skills such as "Psionics" and others.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/13cc9798cfb4cedcdd8ee980e5c34fb610f43d67.jpg[/img]

[b]Every skill available will change accordingly with your profession[/b], skillset and proficiency. This means that an engineer won't likely got the option to use a [b]Heavy Laser Rifl[/b]e, while a doctor will heal himself more by using a [b]medkit [/b]as opposite of a security guard. [b]First Aid[/b] training will improve the number of Hit Points recovered by using a medkit, for example.

Also, every profession will have one or more "combat skills" (the screenshots are showing the "[b]Diplomacy[/b]" one) which will be granted provided you reach a certain number of skill points in a given class (that's why attending classes is important. The Combat Skills are tied to your profession as well, so a Science Officer will likely receive an "[b]Enemy Scan[/b]" feature to show weak points, or a Counselor could use a "[b]Psychological Trick[/b]", while an Engineer could use a "Hacking" skill and so on...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/501fa3f4322c967f2f9ac14b0d8335348c1d790c.jpg[/img]

[b]New fights have been added in the game[/b], whereas they were only lines of text. One of them will have you face The Prophet and his soldiers, provided you chose to fight against them. More fighting situations will be added in the game, to allow you to use your hard-earned skills in different tasks, both aboard a starship and on ground duty.

Update 0.0.20 will introduce this feature in a few weeks. [b]All the screenshots are a work in progress[/b] and will likely change in appearance before the final release. 

In the meantime I would like to receive your suggestions in the comments, or in the dedicated topic on the Steam forums!

[b]Thank you for your support! Always![/b]

Stay safe and healthy,

ANDREA BRUNI

notes.title: Happy new year!
notes.content:
Greetings to all players and community!

This has been an unique year. And I sincerely hope it stays that way.

Many of my projects have suffered a serious delay, both for [b]personal family issues[/b] which I already told you about in the last few months and that are far from being over, and for [b]economical reasons[/b], of course.  The plan to launch a brand-new [b]Kickstarter campaign[/b] in November was halted, as the world and people are still struggling with the pandemic and its effects on our lives.

Development for my games hasn't stopped a bit, but it was delayed as I had to take care of my children and family, especially while schools were closed and they had to stay home. I managed to release many updates and new stories, and in the next few months more will come with[b] a new Otome Visual Novel[/b], new chapters for [b]The Devil's Shoes[/b], improvements on [b]Yomi Alliance[/b], the [b]2nd free DLC for General Practitioner[/b] and[b] two new episodes of The Coroner Saga[/b], which are already written and only need some polish.

New rewards are also available for Patrons on my [url=https://patreon.com/brunimultimedia]Patreon page[/url], and they will keep getting released over and over. I think that would be the best way to thank you for your support, despite my setbacks which are not due to my will but which I apologize for, regardless.

[b]Developing a videogame, even a Visual Novel, is a very costly effort[/b], and you only see results months after you spend those money. For a single-man company like mine this is more than a challenge at times, and that's why [b]I completely rely on your support[/b] and your appreciation of my work to keep doing what I do: develop games to entertain you in the best of times, and in the worst of times.

[b]So, thank you for your support, past, present and future. Without you, there won't be any Bruni Multimedia to talk about and no videogames at all from me.[/b]

I hope you can live a happier year, we're going through this together, as the Doctor told during the "Coronavirus Exam" released last February (my, it's already a full year!).

Happy new year to everyone. Keep following me, because there will be tons of news coming up in the next few days

Stay safe, and healthy!

notes.title: Different tasks for different careers
notes.content:
Greetings fellow space officers!

One of the best features of Yomi Alliance is the ability to play different missions for each different career choice. And by career I don't mean just "Medical" vs "Command", but all the sub-choices you make when starting a new game.

After the mission which introduces you to the "Prophet" character, Captain Marston will instruct you to go in the Command Center and assign you a task. This task will be different for each career, and will unlock new parts of the story. If you play the game with a new character you can explore these different paths.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/5d1d21f8f0c1451d73e3a93b11d0e9578749b535.png[/img]

Are you curious about what you can expect from the first of many different mission paths? Let's dig them in detail!

[b]Starship Commander[/b]
As a future Starship Commander it's up to you to understand the feeling of your companions.
Captain Marston wants you to interview every Recruit in the Academy and file a full report about their thoughts about the attack, their fears, their doubts, their opinions.
    
[b]Diplomatic Representative[/b]
As a future Diplomatic Representative it's up to you to establish relationships with other cultures.
Captain Marston wants you to contact the Nixanti Council and ask them about this Prophet of Alarei.
Reaching the Council won't be easy, as they don't usually grant private audiences. Being a Nixanti could help you somehow...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/5b289258b78989b0b1c82b0a29c0e0d54b1f965e.png[/img]

[b]Manager[/b]
As a future Manager it's up to you to manage Alliance resources with care. Many valuable equipment was stolen or destroyed in the attack.
The Captain wants you to assess the status of weapons and equipment inventory and make arrangements with our suppliers to restore them. If your character has a "Merchant" upbringing he will meet familiar faces during the mission as well.

[b]Navigator[/b]
As a future Navigator you need to know your way around star maps.
The Captain wants you to track the Prophet's ship's flight path throughout Alliance space. As his ship was using some kind of cloaking device that won't be easy though.
    
[b]Hot-Shot Pilot[/b]
As a future Hot-Shot Pilot you will become an expert of shuttle fighters.
The Captain wants you to prepare a flotilla of defensive shuttles and equip them as you see fit.
Next time the Prophet or any of his friends show around, Marston wants every available ship to be ready for them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/2e9b2370a7fdf47206c65303721bb5e5786b9158.jpg[/img]
    
[b]Mechanic[/b]
A lot of equipment is faulty since the attack, communications and food replicators most of all.
As a future Mechanic the Captain wants you to lead the repair crews.

[b]Specialist[/b]
As a future Specialist the Captain wants you to program the computer for a set of safety precautions that will automatically activate in case of a new attack.
    
[b]Starship Designer[/b]
You're going to become a Starship Designer. The Captain wants your help to design a new kind of reconnaissance drone to help security spot hostiles inside academy grounds in case of future attacks.
    
[b]Systems Specialist[/b]
As a future Systems Specialist the Captain wants you to increase sensor efficiency for the next time the Prophet or any of his friends shows around.
    
[b]Basic Operator[/b]
As a Basic Operator the Captain wants you to check if repairs at comm systems, replicators and internal sensors have been completed.
He also wants you to perform a full scan of each system and report any glitch to Engineering.
    
[b]Operations Manager[/b]
As Operations Manager in training the Captain wants you to coordinate repair teams, switching personnel, equipment and priorities for the repairs.
    
[b]Security Officer[/b]
As a Security Officer the Captain wants you to patrol the damaged areas of the Academy.
You received reports of armed civilians trying to loot military equipment from there. Your orders are either to arrest them or scare them off without using deadly force.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/1be53a59c723ffea3fd6d10c5f80043f7b2ba423.png[/img]
    
[b]Investigator[/b]
Security captured one of the assailants. She was left for dead by the Prophet's assault team.
As an Investigator the Captain wants you to lead the interrogation of the prisoner. 
Learn what you can from her by using any means necessary.
    
[b]Tactical Officer[/b]
As a Tactical Officer you're an expert about space tactics and maneuvers.
For that reason the Captain wants you to analyze the flight pattern of the Prophet's ship and learn how it defied Earth's unmanned planetary defenses.
    
[b]Interspecies Relationship Expert[/b]
As an Interspecies Relationship Expert the Captain wants you to study the current relationships between the Kressari, the Nixanti, the Awar and the Karis.
He was surprised they were working together during the attack and he wants to know what changed between their relationship.

[b]Counselor[/b]
As a Counselor The Captain wants you to bring psychological support to the people injured in the attack.
Many of them lost someone important during the fight. The Captain wants you to help them deal with the loss.
Some of them might blame you for some reason (not spoilering anything), so that task might be more difficult than it should.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/388e4281f93b3406e1b9f17b69140492a446c443.png[/img]
    
[b]Alien Specialist[/b]
As an Alien Specialist the Captain wants you to solve a little mystery, especially if you're familiar with Kressari physiology.
Security found a body of a Kressari in the battlefield. It was hit by a direct blast of laser energy and yet there are no burns over it.
Captain Marston wants you to conduct a full analysis of the body and file a full report.
    
[b]Emergency Medic[/b]
As an Emergency Medic the Captain needs you to go to the Infirmary and help Dr. Li treat those who were injured during the attack.

[b]General Practitioner[/b]
As a General Practitioner you are required to perform medical exams on the people who were dismissed from the Infirmary and assess whether they're fit for duty or not.

[b]Scientist[/b]
As a Scientist you will need to prove a theory right or wrong.
Sensors detected thorium particles on the Prophet's ship before it disappeared from sensors.
The Captain needs you to gather data about nearby star systems or spatial phenomena that could've caused the thorium's accumulation.

[b]Science Officer[/b]
As a Science Officer you will need to be ready to unravel every scientific mystery you might encounter.
That technology the Prophet uses is indeed a mystery. The Captain wants you to analyze the data you've got on it and file a full report.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/9469c7a3c40a3a858d3af3a16a0e8b960cf55be2.png[/img]
    
[b]Social Surveyor[/b]
As a Social Surveyor, the Captain wants you to tell him how Nixanti religion spread amongst Kressari, Awar and Karis people.
Do they have anything in common? Do they share the same beliefs?
    
[b]Planetary Surveyor[/b]
As a Planetary Surveyor the Captain wants you to assess any damage the alien weapons could've made to the planet.
He wants you to make sure there are no radiation leaks, surface damage or anything else that would cause any harm to Earth's people.

During those missions you will meet new and old characters, familiarize with console commands, unravel mysteries and discover more about the lore of Yomi universe. Each mission will be full of dialogues, choices and a score will be given to you. You can unlock achievements with that score and that will also influence your final evaluation before you are being transferred to a starship for the second part of the game.

Enjoy Yomi Alliance, enjoy the consequences of your decisions!

notes.title: DEVLOG #5: Medical examinations, Console Setting, Difficulty Level
notes.content:
Greetings fellow space officers!

I have been very busy over the last few weeks to develop the brand new medical simulation for the game. Some of you had a glimpse of it while examining Serena during the first lesson which also introduced Dr. Li, and now you'll get the chance to play a couple more scenarios.

At first I wanted to develop a simple situation: a patient, you, the teacher. While I moved deeper into it though I realized that things could've been more fun if I added some kind of unpredictability.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/e80a5d4209bad08b2df36ac37586479c8bf3184c.png[/img]

[b]Medical Classes[/b]

Dr. Li will introduce a few classes where you will be randomly brought to scan 8 different patients:
- Aberoin, your teammate who kindly volounteered for the simulation
- Hergarr, a 21 years old Awar Female
- Syun-Ho, a 20 years old Karis Female
- Kormash, a 29 years old Kressari Male
- R18-20, a 27 years old Fuminoid Male
- Jowarr, a 39 years old Zalkan Male
- Meshal, a 25 years old Zurian Female
- Say-Gan, a 22 years old Karis Female

There are 20 different, randomly chosen, ailments your simulated patients might face. From Acceplexia Fever to Carmus Flu and Hydroga Aspisis. Of course those are ailments that are unknown to modern human medicine, so you'll have to learn how to recognize them and how to deal with them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/a90a9ac6b92803625cb48d0e45797fb532d20440.png[/img]

Codex Informations are available. They indicate the symptoms of each ailment and its cure, if any. You might need to administer medicines or antidotes, or even wake up a patient from a (simulated) coma.

This will teach medical-career players on how to deal with the medical scanner, which is also animated like many other consoles throughout the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/0a6a62ddf91830cdf104ace81c8b2fc49c477c0f.png[/img]

[b]Wait, I don't want to use the animated console! It's too difficult and annoying![/b]

Worry not! A new setting, called "Console Interaction", is available in the Preferences screen. You can set it on "Simulation" to deal with the animated console or to "Visual Novel" to have a list of choices brought to you in a clickable menu, with the animated console on the back.

You can set the difficulty of the game at any time, except during the simulation, when the choice you made will be brought until its end.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/68aa9119caa26afffd372ca8450ac157fd176549.png[/img]

[b]It's too difficult![/b]
Again, worry not! The difficulty settings have been renamed to "Ensign" being the easiest one, "Lieutenant" being a middle-level and "Captain" being the harder.

If you play on "Captain", for example, Dr. Li will grant you bonus or malus points based on the choices you made during the medical examination. The more useless choices you make the worst his judgement will be. However, some of you might not want to deal with this and prefer a smoother gameplay. By choosing "Ensign" or "Lieutenant" difficulty level you will just end the simulation like a normal in-game event without bad consequences.
You can set the difficulty of the game at any time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/963393b5ef703cfed65176014a9852aae0024286.png[/img]

Difficulty will also influence the chance your energy level will affect your learning ability. If you're too tired there will be a chance you fail to learn anything. The chance will be way lower on "Ensign" difficulty than it will be on "Captain".

I recommend to play the game on "Captain" difficulty if you want a real challenge, but feel free to play it on either setting if you want a moderate challenge or a plain Visual Novel experience.

It was difficult to develop this, but I can't wait for you to play it and give me many feedback about it as well! You will need different playthroughs if you want to explore every possible scenario, as some illnesses will only affect Fuminoids, Kressari, Humans and it will be challenging enough to figure out what a patient's issue is!

Stay with me for more informations about the game's development and new exciting announcements of voice-actors as well!

Stay safe and healthy!

notes.title: Romance paths in Yomi Alliance
notes.content:
Greetings fellow space travelers!

Today I'm going to talk to you about the romance options in Yomi Alliance and the different story paths linked to them.

As you're undoubtedly aware there are four different squad mates you can interact with, and their Relationship Level is shown in the main interface of the game. To increase or decrease that bar you just need to pick up the right choices when presented to you and also increase one specific stat (their "favourite" stat). As long as the romantic relation goes further you can flirt with them, kiss them and even have sex with them as you would in real life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/300fdc5dc667518e55052d0cf1cc181084607551.png[/img]

Of course those interactions are still work in progress, and right now you can only unlock a couple of them, but in time more and more content will be added, included romance-specific side stories to explore and enjoy.

With a brand new voice-over feature that will be introduced before the end of the year (keep following the updates for more excitement about it) I'm sure you'll enjoy the available romance paths in the game.

But the 4 squad mates won't be your only chance to get romantically involved, as three teachers are also going to be available as romantic interests. They won't have a "favourite stat" but they will require their romance options to be unlocked by attending their classes and get a good standing with them, again, with your choices and dialogue options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/d8b9b50ac7faadfcd9e6651092c1becc32832726.png[/img]

The game will feature M/F, M/M, F/F relationships and even genderless ones for Briallen characters.

[b]Male characters [/b]will be able to bond with: Mivak, Serena, Aberoin, Lt. Kaila, Sulijan, Lt. Mkrell

[b]Female characters[/b] will be able to bond with: Sulijan, Aberoin, Lt. Mkrell, Dr. Li

[b]Genderless Briallen characters[/b] will be able to bond with: Aberoin, Lt. Kaila, Dr. Li, Mivak, Serena, Lt. Mkrell

As you can see each NPC has its own gender preference as in real life. Serena for example isn't attracted by women, while Mivak has no issue with any gender or species and neither does Aberoin. Sulijan isn't attracted by Briallen and so on.

Each romance will develop its own path, so next time you start a new playthrough in Yomi Alliance you can experiment a brand new path and many new situations in game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/17cb255a4a9676c43371d62a5a94892c1ee031da.png[/img]

I hope you'll enjoy the romantic choices available and always remember that you can befriend a character not available as a romance partner: many conversations will unlock regardless, since you'll be friends.

Thank you for your support of the game and its development! Stay with me for more news in a few days!

Stay safe and healthy,

notes.title: The current COVID-19 situation and our games
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

It's very strange to write this stuff, but I think you deserve to know the behind-the-scenes of the current situation in Italy, the place where I live and work.

The lockdown announced by the government fortunately doesn't include my job, so I can keep developing all my games (as you can see by the updates I published yesterday and the day before).

However, it would be false to state that it doesn't affect my production at all. The streets are empty as they are on holiday weeks, right now I can still access my office but I don't know for how long (I can still work from home, but it would be VERY difficult), plus I'm overall concerned for my family and kids, and writing videogames with that kind of mental stress is sometimes difficult. But I'm trying to do my best, as I always did. And I just hope the situation won't be worse than this in the future.

Plus, with most services out of order and the invitation to go out by oneself and without other family members, I have to take care of many things personally, which is something that takes time and it's a time I can't work at all (buying groceries, bills, managing bank accounts, buying medicines and playing with my kids since the schools are closed).

So, some updates of the game could be delivered with a delay in the near future. I am VERY sorry about this and believe me I'm doing the best I can to ensure you'll receive everything smoothly as I always did in the last three years (BTW, the 3-year anniversary for General Practitioner is coming on May and there will be surprises for everyone!)

That's it. I just wanted you to know the current situation and why I'm more silent than ever on social media channels: right now all my energies are focused on developing stories, not talking about them.

Thank you for your support. I hope this situation will defuse soon and without long-lasting consequences. BTW for those of you who still don't know I published a "Coronavirus Update" on General Practitioner a while ago. It's not meant to inform people about the situation, it's just meant to smile and be a "doctor Casanova" despite everything :)

Be safe and healthy, now more than ever!

ANDREA BRUNI

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/71d1c621f0cc872b1bb22a6237e25dc81e454ca8.png[/img]

I hope you'll enjoy the new content in the game. It adds some new gameplay options as well as some new stories to explore. Alongside a new Codex interface for important lore informations, Yomi Alliance is taking shape update after update, with most release-bugs now gone.

notes.title: Meet the Briallen
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/3b4bb68d009687388d0b1a27c62e4dcad8e680fb.png[/img]

[b]PERSONALITY:[/b] Most Briallen are peaceful, contemplative people who simply wish to live in peace with their neighbors. Their peculiar biology, however, is source of misunderstanding and prejudice amongst other species, even though Yomi Founders' species (Humans, Nixanti and Fuminoids) always welcomed the Briallen into their society.
As a result of the major distrust towards them, many Briallen turned into ruthless, passionate people willing to do anything to protect their homeworld from threats to its independence and security.
Recently, the Briallen Hierarchy started to pursue Alliance Membership trough diplomatic channels, even though many independendists seek to stop this important step, stating it would thwart Briallen's quest for independence and freedom.

[b]PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION:[/b] Briallen possess the same average height, weight, and variations in skin tone and hair color as Humans. The only outward physical difference is the presence of both genders' genitalia. They prefer loose-fitting clothes in a variety of earth tones and other subdued colors when dealing with outsiders to hide their different biology, while when between friends or people of the same species they usually wear nothing at all. 
Many of them also possess distinctive tattoos to display their devotion to their Gods (the Briars). In times past, the design of the tattoo also revealed a Briallen's social status, but many modern Briallen have discarded that tradition. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/4833c17eef5ae9f985f2665b6bdeb53dc5f86735.png[/img]

[b]HOMEWORLD:[/b] Furatu, the third of eleven planets orbiting Briar'va'el, is a pleasant world similar in most respects to Earth.

[b]CULTURE:[/b] Briallen culture began approximately 60,000 years ago. Through four multiple-millennia republics, periods of civil wars and chaos, and a brutal war against their first-contact species, the Galixians, it has remained largely unified and coherent. The Briallen religion, which has become less and less important in their culture, centers on the worship of Briars, genderless gods who, according to legends, never interacted with the Briallen population over the centuries.

Regardless of religion, every Briallen tries to live peacefully and aims to be useful to other people in their society and in the Alliance. Their government is an an elaborate hierarchy where every citizen has the right to participate if they wish so.
Briallen people are also renown for their culinary skills. From cooking both home and exotic foods, the Briallen produce tastes envied and admired by many other civilizations. Food industry plays a large role in Briallen's economy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/4fecb56dcd1bb47cc100e82918a564616c778e85.jpg[/img]

[b]NEUTRAL PRONOUN: [/b]As Briallen are a hermaphrodit species, it is polite not to refer to them as "Him" or "Her", as the neutral pronoun "Hem" is used widely amongst them. At the same time "his" and "her" are translated into "shem" (or "sher" by some dialectal forms), and "He"/"She" is translated into "Shes".
As aliens often strive to use the proper word, Briallen learned not to be offended by other species' mistakes, as long as the mistake is genuine and not meant to be disrespecftul.

Briallen's sexual preferences have always been somewhat a myth amongst non-Briallen. People always think that a Briallen is bisexual and has no sexual preference. While the majority of the population shows no issues in mating with other Briallen, alien multi-gendered species attract Briallen differently. About 40% of Briallen people claim to be attracted by females of alien species, another 40% by males and a 10% claims to find aliens "disgusting".

It is considered rude to ask a Briallen about their sexual preference directly, unless they're on a close relationship with you.

notes.title: DEVLOG #4: Developing your skills
notes.content:
Greetings fellow officers!

Today I'm going to introduce you on the different ways to acquire skills in Yomi Alliance, which is hopefully a fun, non-grinding way to achieve your objectives and increase your character's stats.

Like some of you already played in the demo, each week you are going to schedule your activities, choosing to pursue your social interests, your training and/or attending classes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/df3ee1c2263dbad748471bcf282a4ce327b282ff.png[/img]

Attending classes will raise your stats from the starting point up to 13 points. While some classes are automatic (you increase your points without any other interaction), many others will feature an in-game event as well.
Let's take three skills for example: [b]Psychology [/b]training for Counselor career and [b]Inquire [/b]training for Security Officers and finally [b]Diplomacy [/b]for the Command School candidate.

As for Psychology your teacher, Counselor Lapp, will ask you questions about simulated patients. You will need to listen to her question carefully, and also deal with patients who are going to tell you about their problems and try the best way to solve them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/300fdc5dc667518e55052d0cf1cc181084607551.png[/img]
You will increase your Stats while also playing the role you chose when starting the game.

[b]Inquire [/b]is a little different. While it plays the same dialogue-choice-consequence pattern, you will be tasked with a real interview of an alien volounteer with his own mini-storyline taking place. Your choices won't just grant you skill points but will develop a shady sub-plot which will finally unveil in the last class session.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/13cf22b1cc0770aa1ba41f4efcfc3e2040070150.png[/img]

Even [b]Diplomacy [/b]aims to bring you a different point of view. This time you will take the role of a famous Fuminoid Captain of the past in a Virtual Reality environment and you will be tasked to negotiate peace within two warring factions. Your choices could bring more chaos into their society or end up with a long-lasting peace treaty and Alliance application.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/9c4487247fa9089e6da7ab038a0f52ded3d1e342.png[/img]

Your character will learn the best way to handle first contact with an alien species directly on the field.

You can expect varied stories and gameplay for many different skills as each update is released. The first Early Access update features dozens of events, social time with Serena, a couple sex scenes, an academy storyline with many events and so on. 

The whole point of different career paths is to get you something different each time you play Yomi Alliance. Psychology classes, for example, are just for the "Counseling" career and related professions, so you might not play any of them on your first playthrough.

As you will start a new game and choose new paths, species and background you will unlock more and more events, many of which you never saw before!

Of course the game will get more content update after update, but there's enough stuff to keep you entertained for many hours right away.

[b]Yomi Alliance will hit Steam's Early Access on February 10th, 2020![/b] Wishlist it today and keep following us!

Thank you for your support!

Be safe and healthy,

notes.title: Playable Species: Meet the Nixanti
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/3c6b96287514b15ab18d8054e79fb9c5c7ef75a3.png[/img]

[b]PERSONALITY[/b]
Most other species regard Nixanti as aggressive, harsh, and xenophobic, but also capable of great cleverness and cunning. Nixanti prefer to deal with others from positions of strength whenever possible, whether that strength be military, intellectual or social.

[b]PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION [/b]
Humanoids, Nixanti possess a wide variety of skin tones and colors amongst males, while females are usually very different and white-skinned. Males skin ranges from green to blue to plain white, and they possess an exoskeleton over their spine. Females, on the other hand, are quite attractive to other species, and don't possess the exoskeleton. They are as tall as but slightly heavier and more muscled than Humans.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/8dfeb08156976cbcf4460b7373271a730dc71b58.png[/img]

[b]HOMEWORLD[/b] 
Nixxia, the third of six planets orbiting the star Noshan.

[b]CULTURE [/b]
The Nixanti possess a rich, vibrant culture, based on the laws derived from ancient Laws passed from generation to generation. Their society puts heavy importance on social status and position, and it's divided into two main groups: Nobleborn ([i]Kotosha[/i]) and Commoners ([i]Arosha[/i]).
Rules of Nixanti society revolve around Four Sacred Laws, given by their profet and demi-god Alarei in person thousands of years ago.
The First Law ([i]grammorkai[/i]) outlines Nixanti relationships between themselves, even if it now applies to alien relationships as well. Nixanti take great pride in their own code of honor, and they will do everything they can to look honorable to other species.
The Second Law ([i]numokai[/i]) describes relationships between Nixxia's government and military personnel. Some observers note that Nixxia never suffered a civil war or any coup-d'etat because of this Law.
The Third Law ([i]satakai[/i]) defines the principles of Nixanti religion. Almost every Nixanti believes in the Seven Gods and their prophet Alarei, although more and more people, especially amongst younglings, are now questioning some parts of their religious education.
The Fourth Law ([i]jenokkai[/i]) enumerates the privileges and responsibilities of Nixanti-Kotosha.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/dfc251f6eb02421d47ae3a219a4258ddb42b15b1.png[/img]

As for the [i]Numokai [/i]rule, the military dominate Nixxia.
 
Sometimes harsh and aggressive, after discovering FTL speed the Nixanti quickly started an imperialistic campaign on habitable worlds within a few light years from their home planet. Their first encounter with the Humans led to an sixteen-year-long war. Similarly, they approached their early encounters with the Fuminoid with suspicion and mistrust, perhaps seeing them as a competitor for resources and hindrance on their ability to expand.

This militaristic culture defines a Nixanti's social status, even though an [i]Arosha [/i]can never be raised to [i]Kotosha [/i]status. However, their culture puts great value on personal skills and talent, and it's not uncommon in recent times that Nixanti-[i]Arosha [/i]command units of Nixanti-[i]Kotosha[/i].

Nixanti society is also a patriarcal one. Males command over females most of the time, even though that's also influenced by social status. Women have the same rights of men on paper, but they need to work twice to earn the same respect and responsibilities of their male counterparts. This is called "[i]res'jan[/i]", and it's a principle that states that every female has to kneel down to a man if they ask to, but only if the man outranks the female in both social and military rank.
While the [i]res'jan[/i] has been declared illegal by Yomi Alliance laws and more and more people refuse to kneel down, the [i]grammorkai[/i] is quite specific in which is the most honorable attitude towards it.
As a result, the [i]res'jan[/i] is still followed by some Nixanti Alliance officers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/dddf536aa51f0845ac03123854eed1ebcf0e5057.png[/img]

[b]FAVORED PROFESSION[/b]: Security Officers. 
Most Nixanti proudly serve the Nixanti Military, thwarting enemy aggression and extending the boundaries of their empire through exploration and conquest. As members of Yomi Alliance, though, each new colony has to be established with Fuminoid and Human approval first. While the Alliance rarely opposes a Nixanti colony on an empty, habitable world, there have been some issues when Nixanti claims landed on previously-occupied worlds such as Charma IV.
While the [i]grammorkai[/i] bounds Nixanti to always recognize their treaties, some fringes of the Nixanti Military have been expressing concerns over something that's perceived as "undue interference in Nixxia's business".

notes.title: The Engineering Officer
notes.content:
Engineers are highly specialized operations officers trained to keep systems and equipment running at max­imum efficiency. They are responsible for shipwide sys­tems, such as the electroplasma system, the FTL drive, and the core engines, as well as repairing individual systems.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/aba4fa10b64acf7606e3eb88a53e661d0a82cc1f.png[/img]

They repair equipment damaged by ion storms or battle damage, calibrate lateral sensors and engine injectors, cobble equipment together from scratch, and generally make sure everything runs without a hitch.

As experts in the practical application of science and mathematics, engineers play a vital role in most missions. When confronted with strange alien technol­ogy-ancient androids, mind transference devices, time machines-the engineer has the best chance of understanding how it works and devising ways to defeat it.

During exploration missions, their skills may be required to find pragmatic solutions to unusual haz­ards-discovering the cause of a space funnel, relieving tectonic pressure on an unstable world, escaping a booby trap, or defeating an insane, intelligent computer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/9901fd8104b0c16001e2cc7a52ec8f160a2087a5.png[/img]

Good at problem-solving, the engineer finds a way to track an hidden ship, escape the grasp of a godlike being, or reinitialize the FTL drive in minutes.

On defensive missions, they are indispensable for repairing battle damage, getting crit­ical systems back on line, and squeezing out the last hit of efficiency from ship's systems."
No matter the adven­ture, when unique solutions are called for, the engineer stands at the ready.

Intellect is the favored attribute of engineers, since they regularly apply scientific princi­ples to practical applications. As with all starship offi­cers, Agility, Strength, and Vitality make good choices for the character's second favored attribute (especially for those who plan to see a lot of action). Dangerous radiation, hazardous materials, and potentially life-threaten­ing situations (such as coolant leaks) make Stamina the engineer's favored reaction.

notes.title: DEVELOPMENT LOG #1: RPG ELEMENTS
notes.content:
Greetings Alliance Officers.

The first Development Log of many (someone might say too many, still I think they're both interesting and a testament to my commitment to the game) will focus on the [b]RPG elements[/b] of Yomi Alliance.

While even in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/936960/General_Practitioner/]General Practitioner[/url] the Main Character had some stats to increase and manage, it was not really an RPG, because skills improvement did unlock some special opportunities, but the story went more or less the same. That was made to[b] avoid transforming the game in a grind fest[/b], something that many adult games around the Internet tend to do a little too often  in my opinion.

The focus of Yomi Alliance's skill increase is to [b]avoid grinding at all costs[/b], because let's just say it: grinding is boring. There's no way I can enjoy repeating the same activity again and again until I put some minor increase in my character's stats or equipment. What we're trying to do is making the character's growth as smooth as possible.

That's why Stats raising will play in the first part of the game: [b]Academy Training[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/df3ee1c2263dbad748471bcf282a4ce327b282ff.png[/img]

[b]Players will attend Yomi Alliance's Navy Academy[/b], a 24 weeks tour of duty where they will learn to be whatever they wish to be. Each different class will attend different classes, like a Science Officer will attend Planetary or Geology classes that Starship Commanders won't, or Counselors-to-be will attend psychology classes unlike their Security Officers counterparts.

Every week you will choose which classes to attend (if any) and a partially-random related-stat will increase accordingly, or you can focus in increasing your relationship with other Squad Members, or just relax and enjoy the sun. [b]The choice is yours.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/ae94abdb4b0c0ad14ac336928df7897644653967.png[/img]

Also, when attending a class an in-game event might trigger, meaning conversations, mini-games and even [b]interactive, fully animated consoles[/b] to press buttons onto.

What happens when you don't study enough or study too hard? Of course, the related Stat will be lower than recommended, or very high and this means... a different playthrough. Yes, because every stat-check is partially random as well, and there's a mathematical calculation based on both Characters' skills and players' choice as well.

This calculation determines if an action was successful or not, and [b]it could hinder, for example, an investigation attempt,[/b] making the game behave in two very different ways in future missions.

Of course branches of the game are also determined by [b]well-thought choices[/b] from players as well, the game won't be randomized that much. It's as there are two possibilities:

- Early decisions made in the Academy will determine the outcome during Starship Duty
- Mid-late game decisions made on the starship are made directly and affect the outcome as well

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36027277/3ad34076fd6ba1914394280c653e65623c82da37.png[/img]

With [b]more than 30 different skills[/b], the storytelling possibilities are countless, and that's how we plan to deliver an almost completely different experience based on your very first choice of the game: [b]who are you going to be in Yomi Alliance[/b]?

Wish to support the game? Get ready for our [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/brunimultimedia/yomi-alliance-an-epic-sci-fi-visual-novel][b]Kickstarter[/b][/url] on October 31st, alongside the release of the Demo!

notes.title: Where are we going next... Support this game!
notes.content:
Greetings fellow doctors!

As General Practitioner is approaching its Beta and Final Release due in December, we started planning our game development future for the foreseeable future, and we're excited to announce you a few projects we have in store, the first of which will be Alpha-Ready when GP will be finalized.

2020 will be full of projects I'm very excited about:
- [b]Yomi Alliance[/b]: a sci-fi Adult RPG/Visual Novel (see next)
- [b]The Coroner Saga[/b]: Episodes 3, 4 and 5
- New DLCs and updates for [b]General Practitioner[/b], many of which for free
- [b]The Devil's Shoes[/b], a brand new 8 hours long erotic videogame
- [b]The Interview[/b], a General Practitioner erotic spinoff 6 hours long

While some of our projects will be announced on a later date, today I want you to know about [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1160950/Yomi_Alliance/]Yomi Alliance[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33586573/3ad34076fd6ba1914394280c653e65623c82da37.png[/img]

This project is ambitious, even bigger than General Practitioner. You can see informations about it on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1160950/Yomi_Alliance/][b]Steam Page[/b][/url] and the [url=www.yomialliance.space][b]Official Website[/b][/url]

Featuring dozens of hours of gameplay, you will experience a different game every time you run a playthrough, since every career choice and even your starting species will determine different outcomes in conversations, actual gameplay and situations!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33586573/22a3387c3f308b85275762cac3150aecb5111e3b.png[/img]

A project this big will need some time to be completed of course, and a lot of money as well. That's why we're starting the Alpha Early Access in December and we're also launching a [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/brunimultimedia/yomi-alliance-an-epic-sci-fi-visual-novel]Kickstarter[/url] for the project on October 31st!

Supporting us on Kickstarter and/or [url=www.patreon.com/generalpractitioner]Patreon[/url] ensures us to keep doing our job: creating different kinds of Visual Novels and make you enjoy them for many hours for the months to come!
All Patreon rewards have been changed to reflect the new releases, so you can take a look to them as well, even though of course the Kickstarter crowdfunding is the best way to show us your support (and earn a Free Steam Key as well).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33586573/9b69f7573ec3a7540fc5593b14d60d62bcc1679d.png[/img]

[b]You can apply for the Kickstarter from October 31st to November 30th, 2019[/b].

[b]A DEMO of the game will be available on October 31st[/b] on Steam as well. The demo will feature the first fours Academy Weeks and one of the first Away Missions. You can choose any of the four species and three genders in the demo and a career of your choice between Command and Science.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33586573/df3ee1c2263dbad748471bcf282a4ce327b282ff.png[/img]

Alpha release in December will feature a FULL Academy training section (about 20+ hours of gameplay) and every month we'll release further content with priority release for our crowdfunders.

We're very excited about this opportunity, we hope you'll keep following us, supporting us and always be safe and healthy!

Thank you.
